notes: BATCH_010 Banking and Financial Awareness, topic package 1 (Banking Fundamentals, History of Banking in India, Reserve Bank of India, RBI Functions, Monetary Policy, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, Bank Rate, Inflation): 68 original questions, IDs BANK_BFA_001802 to BANK_BFA_001869. Built from RBI pages opened on 2026-11-06 (consolidated Commercial Banks Directions of 28 Nov 2025 on deposits, advances and voluntary amalgamation, the Miscellaneous Directions' DEA Fund chapter, the liquidity management framework of 30 Sep 2025, MPC resolutions Feb 2025-Oct 2026, RBI press releases and auction results, FAQs on currency, cheque clearing and Government banking, RBI's history chronology, Governors' profiles and Bank Rate/CRR/SLR table) and MoSPI/DPIIT price releases. Only current rules are tested; older rules appear only as explicit history. Computed answers are re-derived with asserts in tools/packages/BFA_pkg1.py. ai:independent-check marks only questions a separate fresh solver answered blind and matched with confidence.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In November 1973, after the nationalisation of the major banks, what change did RBI's chronology record for the State Bank of India and its subsidiaries?

options.text: They were merged into a single bank
Restrictions on them were removed to bring them on par with other commercial banks
They were brought under the Lead Bank Scheme for the first time
They were barred from opening rural branches

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology for November 1973 records that restrictions on SBI and its subsidiaries were removed to bring them on par with other commercial banks.
steps: Nov 1973 → restrictions on SBI group removed (parity with other banks)
solution.why_others_wrong: The associates merged with SBI only in 2017; the Lead Bank Scheme dates from 1969; rural branch expansion was encouraged, not barred.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Restrictions on them were removed to bring them on par with other commercial banks

fact_checks.claim: Nov 1973: Restrictions on SBI and its subsidiaries removed to bring them on par with other commercial banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Through which portal must banks submit the information and documents required for RBI's approval of a voluntary amalgamation under the Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025?

solution.explanation: After shareholders approve the scheme, it is submitted to RBI for sanction; the information and documents are filed through RBI's PRAVAAH portal (pravaah.rbi.org.in).
steps: Scheme approved by Boards and shareholders
solution.why_others_wrong: CIMS is RBI's statistical returns system; Sachet is for complaints about unauthorised deposit-taking; Daksh is RBI's supervisory application.
solution.final_answer: Option D: PRAVAAH

fact_checks.claim: information and documents shall be submitted to RBI through the PRAVAAH portal (https://pravaah.rbi.org.in)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In his statement of 7 October 2026, the RBI Governor announced a new committee to serve as a forum for structured engagement with market participants and other stakeholders on policy and operational matters relating to financial markets. What is it called?

options.text: Standing Advisory Committee on Money Markets
Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets
Financial Stability and Development Council Sub-Committee

solution.explanation: Citing rapidly evolving financial market dynamics, the Governor said RBI would constitute a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets as a forum for structured engagement with market participants and other stakeholders on policy and operational matters related to financial markets.
steps: October 2026 announcement → Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets
solution.why_others_wrong: The Financial Markets Committee is RBI's internal committee that reviews liquidity daily; the other two are not what was announced.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's profile of Governor S. Jagannathan (1970–1975) links his tenure to which development flowing from one of the important objectives of bank nationalisation?

options.text: An exponential expansion of banking offices
The merger of the SBI associate banks
The introduction of the Base Rate system
The first issue of RBI's own banknotes

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the 'One State-One RRB' amalgamation, RBI notified (Gazette of 11 November 2025) that 8 Regional Rural Banks were included in and 19 erstwhile RRBs excluded from the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, and (Gazette of 3 February 2026) that 3 RRBs were included and 7 erstwhile RRBs excluded. What was the net reduction in the number of RRBs in the Second Schedule from these two notifications?

solution.concept: Second Schedule changes from RRB amalgamation
solution.explanation: Each amalgamation removes the erstwhile RRBs from the Second Schedule and adds the new amalgamated RRB. Net reduction = (19 − 8) + (7 − 3) = 11 + 4 = 15.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11 and 4 are each notification alone; 37 adds inclusions instead of subtracting them.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 15

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's chronology, the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (II of 1934), which constitutes the statutory basis of the Bank, is dated:

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology lists 5 March 1934 for the RBI Act, 1934 (II of 1934), 'the statutory basis on which the Bank is established'. The Bank commenced operations on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 April 1935 is when operations began; 1 January 1949 is nationalisation; 26 January 1934 is not a date in the chronology.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 5 March 1934

fact_checks.claim: 5 March 1934: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, (II of 1934) constitutes the statutory basis on which the Bank is established

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: N. C. Sen Gupta was RBI Governor for about three months in 1975 until K. R. Puri could take over. What post was he holding before his appointment?

options.text: Chairman of the State Bank of India
India's Executive Director at the IMF
Secretary to the Department of Banking, Ministry of Finance

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about Shri Rohit Jain's appointment as Deputy Governor of RBI in May 2026:
I. The Government appointed him under Section 8(1)(a) read with Section 8(4) of the RBI Act, 1934, for three years from the date of joining on or after 3 May 2026, or until further orders.
II. He was an Executive Director of RBI at the time of his appointment.
III. In the portfolio distribution effective 4 May 2026 he was given the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Government's notification of 2 May 2026 appointed 'Shri Rohit Jain, Executive Director' as Deputy Governor under Section 8(1)(a) read with 8(4), for three years from joining on or after 3 May 2026 (I, II). In the portfolio list of 4 May 2026 the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems is with Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu; Shri Jain's portfolios include the Department of Government and Bank Accounts and the Financial Markets Regulation Department, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – DPSS is with Shri Murmu
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'II only' leaves out the true statement I.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 8 of the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934, read with sub-section (4) of section 8 thereof, has appointed Shri Rohit Jain, Executive Director as Deputy Governor ... for a period of three years from the date of joining the post on or after May 03, 2026 or until further orders

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about meetings of RBI's Central Board in 2026:
I. The 621st meeting was held in New Delhi in February 2026, after which the Union Finance Minister addressed the Directors on the Union Budget 2026-27.
II. The 622nd meeting, held in Patna in March 2026, approved RBI's budget for 2026-27 and its Medium Term Strategy Framework 'Utkarsh 3.0' for 2026-29.
III. Both meetings were chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The 621st meeting (New Delhi, 23 February 2026) was followed by the Finance Minister's address on the Budget (I). The 622nd meeting (Patna, 20 March 2026) approved the Bank's 2026-27 budget and Utkarsh 3.0 for 2026-29 (II). Both were chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra; the Finance Minister only addressed the Directors after the 621st meeting, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – the Governor chairs the Central Board
solution.why_others_wrong: The Central Board is chaired by the Governor, so options with III are wrong; 'II only' leaves out I.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The 621 st meeting of the Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India was held today at New Delhi under the Chairmanship of Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor ... Smt. The 622 nd meeting of the Central Board ... was held today in Patna under the Chairmanship of Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor ... The Board approved the Bank's budget for the accounting year 2026-27 and also the Bank's Medium Term Strategy Framework (Utkarsh 3.0) for the period 2026-29

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's profiles of its Governors:
I. R. N. Malhotra had served as an Executive Director of the IMF before he became Governor.
II. S. Jagannathan relinquished the Governorship to take up the post of India's Executive Director at the IMF.
III. Dr. Y. V. Reddy was India's Executive Director at the World Bank immediately before becoming Governor.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Governors and the Bretton Woods institutions

Jagannathan 'relinquished office to take up the post of the Indian Executive Director at the IMF' (II). questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What is the purpose of RBI's Mobile Aided Note Identifier (MANI) app?

options.text: To verify whether a banknote is genuine or counterfeit
To report counterfeit notes to the police
To locate the nearest currency chest
To help visually impaired persons identify the denomination of a banknote; it does not check genuineness

solution.concept: RBI's tools for the visually impaired
solution.explanation: MANI is a free RBI app that identifies the denomination of MG Series and MG (New) Series notes, even half-folded and in low light, without needing the internet. RBI notes that it does not authenticate a note as genuine or counterfeit.
solution.why_others_wrong: It does not authenticate notes, report counterfeits or locate currency chests.
solution.final_answer: Option D: To help visually impaired persons identify the denomination of a banknote; it does not check genuineness

fact_checks.claim: Mobile Aided Note Identifier (MANI) is a mobile application launched by the Reserve Bank for aiding visually impaired persons to identify the denomination of Indian Banknotes ... This mobile application does not authenticate a note as being either genuine or counterfeit

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the old Indian coinage system recalled in RBI's 'Anecdotes and Trivia', how many pies made one rupee?

solution.explanation: 3 pies made a pice, 4 pice an anna and 16 annas a rupee, so a rupee was 3 × 4 × 16 = 192 pies. Minting of the copper pie was discontinued after 1942.
solution.why_others_wrong: 64 is the number of pice in a rupee; 16 the number of annas; 100 paise came with decimal coinage.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 192

fact_checks.claim: 3 pies made a pice; 4 pice made an anna and 16 annas made a rupee. One rupee, thus consisted of 192 pies

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Banking Companies Act, 1949, which formed the statutory basis of bank supervision and regulation in India, was later renamed as the:

options.text: Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology says the Banking Companies Act, 1949, which came into force on 16 March 1949, formed the statutory basis of bank supervision and regulation and was later renamed the Banking Regulation Act.
steps: Banking Companies Act, 1949 → renamed Banking Regulation Act
solution.why_others_wrong: The RBI Act (1934) is a separate law; the other two are different statutes.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Banking Regulation Act

fact_checks.claim: Coming into force of the Banking Companies Act, 1949. This formed the statutory basis of bank supervision and regulation in India ... The Banking Companies Act was later renamed the Banking Regulation Act

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's currency FAQs, in which year were banknotes with the legend 'Satyameva Jayate' introduced for the first time?

solution.explanation: The first note of independent India was the one-rupee note of 1949; names and the guarantee clause appeared in Hindi from 1951; high denominations returned in 1954; notes with 'Satyameva Jayate' (truth alone shall prevail) were introduced for the first time in 1970; the Mahatma Gandhi series came in 1996.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1949 is the first one-rupee note of independent India; 1954 the return of ₹1000/₹5000/₹10000; 1996 the MG series.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 1970

fact_checks.claim: In the year 1970, banknotes with the legend "Satyameva Jayate", i.e., truth alone shall prevail were introduced for the first time

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What does the 'I promise to pay the bearer the sum of …' clause on a banknote signify, according to RBI?

options.text: RBI's obligation, under Section 26 of the RBI Act, to pay the value of the note to the holder on demand
A promise by the Government to redeem the note in gold
The personal guarantee of the Governor who signed it
That the note can be exchanged only at the bank that issued it

solution.explanation: Under Section 26 of the RBI Act, RBI is liable to pay the value of a banknote, payable on demand by RBI as the issuer. The promissory clause denotes this obligation towards the holder.
steps: Section 26 → RBI liable for value of note → promissory clause
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no gold convertibility; the signature is official, not a personal guarantee; notes are not tied to any particular bank.
solution.final_answer: Option A: RBI's obligation, under Section 26 of the RBI Act, to pay the value of the note to the holder on demand

fact_checks.claim: As per Section 26 of Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Bank is liable to pay the value of banknote. This is payable on demand by RBI, being the issuer. The promissory clause ... denotes the obligation on the part of the Bank towards the holder of the bank note

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Model Co-op. Bank Ltd. was included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934 by a notification published in the Gazette on 11 November 2025. What does inclusion in the Second Schedule make a bank?

solution.explanation: Banks included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act are 'scheduled banks'. RBI announced on 2 December 2025 that Model Co-op. Bank Ltd. had been included by its notification of 20 October 2025, published in the Gazette on 11 November 2025.
solution.why_others_wrong: Systemic importance is a separate (D-SIB) framework; inclusion does not change the bank's type or exempt it from CRR.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A scheduled bank

fact_checks.claim: "Model Co-op. Bank Ltd." has been included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 vide Notification ... dated October 20, 2025 and published in the Gazette of India ... dated November 11, 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the angular bleed lines and identification marks on Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series banknotes, according to RBI's FAQs:
I. The ₹100 note has 4 angular bleed lines in 2 blocks.
II. The ₹500 note has 5 angular bleed lines in 3 blocks.
III. The size of the identification marks on notes of ₹100 and above was increased by 25 per cent.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Angular bleed lines: 4 lines in 2 blocks on ₹100, 4 lines with two circles in between on ₹200, 5 lines in 3 blocks on ₹500 and 7 on ₹2000 (I, II). The identification marks on ₹100 and above were enlarged by 50 per cent, not 25, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Angular Bleed Lines have been introduced in banknotes - 4 lines in 2 blocks in ₹100, 4 angular bleed lines with two circles in between in ₹200, 5 lines in 3 blocks in ₹500, 7 in ₹2000*. In addition, the size of the identification marks in denominations ₹100 and above have been increased by 50 percent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A term deposit matures on a Sunday and is paid on Monday. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what interest is due for the Sunday?

options.text: Interest at the originally contracted rate on the original principal for that day
No interest, since the deposit had matured
Interest at the savings deposit rate
Interest at the bank's current term deposit rate for one day

solution.explanation: If a term deposit matures on a non-business working day, the bank pays interest at the originally contracted rate on the original principal for the intervening non-business day(s) up to payment on the next working day. For reinvestment and recurring deposits, such interest is paid on the maturity value.
steps: Maturity on holiday → contracted rate for the gap day(s)
solution.why_others_wrong: Interest is not nil, nor at the savings rate or a new card rate.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Interest at the originally contracted rate on the original principal for that day

fact_checks.claim: If a term deposit is maturing for payment on a non-business working day, a bank shall pay interest at the originally contracted rate on the original principal deposit amount for the non-business working day, intervening between the date of the maturity ... and the date of payment ... on the succeeding working day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which institution, established in July 1988 according to RBI's chronology, is the apex body of housing finance in India?

options.text: Discount and Finance House of India
Small Industries Development Bank of India

solution.why_others_wrong: HUDCO is a Government company for housing projects; DFHI (April 1988) is a money market institution; SIDBI serves small industries.

fact_checks.claim: Jul 1988: The National Housing Bank established as an apex body of housing finance and to promote activities in housing development
Apr 1988: The Discount and Finance House of India, set up as a money market institution, commenced operations

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The State Financial Corporations Act, 1951, which came into effect on 1 August 1952, enabled State Governments to set up financial corporations mainly for meeting the credit needs of:

solution.explanation: According to RBI's chronology, the SFC Act enabled States to establish financial corporations for the credit needs of medium and small scale industries; RBI's holdings in SFC capital were taken over by IDBI in 1976.
steps: SFCs → medium and small industry credit
solution.why_others_wrong: SFCs were not meant for large PSUs, co-operatives or foreign trade finance.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Medium and small scale industries

fact_checks.claim: 1 Aug 1952: State Financial Corporations Act, 1951 came into effect. It Enabled state governments to establish Financial corporations for meeting the credit needs of medium and small scale industries

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, floating rate domestic term deposits must be linked to:

options.text: A directly observable and transparent market-determined external benchmark
The Bank Rate published by RBI

solution.explanation: The Directions require floating rate domestic term deposits to be linked to a directly observable and transparent market-determined external benchmark.
steps: Floating rate TD → external, market-determined benchmark
solution.why_others_wrong: Internal rates such as MCLR or the bank's savings rate are not allowed; the Bank Rate is not specified.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A directly observable and transparent market-determined external benchmark

fact_checks.claim: Floating rate domestic term deposits shall be linked to a directly observable and transparent market determined external benchmark

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under continuous clearing in CTS, a drawee bank must confirm a presented cheque before its 'Item Expiry Time'. According to RBI's FAQs, can this time be extended?

options.text: Yes, by the drawee bank at its own discretion for any cheque above ₹5 lakh
Yes, by one or more hours or days in extraordinary circumstances, with RBI's approval
No, it can never be extended
Yes, at the request of the payee

solution.concept: Item Expiry Time in continuous clearing
solution.explanation: Item Expiry Time is the latest time for the drawee bank's confirmation, after which the cheque is deemed approved. RBI's FAQs say it may be extended for one or more hours/days in extraordinary circumstances with the approval of the Reserve Bank.
steps: Extension possible only in extraordinary circumstances + RBI approval
solution.why_others_wrong: Drawee banks and payees cannot extend it themselves, and it is not absolutely fixed.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Yes, by one or more hours or days in extraordinary circumstances, with RBI's approval

fact_checks.claim: Item Expiry Time of cheque/s may be extended for one or more hours / days in extraordinary circumstances with approval of the Reserve Bank of India

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: If a cheque is lost in transit or in the clearing process, what should the collecting bank do, according to RBI's FAQs on cheque clearing?

options.text: Debit the drawer's account using the cheque's image
Ask the drawee bank to pay the cheque without the instrument
Immediately inform the presenting customer (beneficiary), so that he can ask the drawer to record stop payment

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say the bank should immediately bring the loss to the beneficiary's notice, so that the customer can inform the drawer to record stop payment and can take care that other cheques issued in anticipation of the credit are not dishonoured.
steps: Inform beneficiary at once → drawer records stop payment
solution.why_others_wrong: Delay is not allowed, and the bank cannot collect on a lost instrument by itself.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Immediately inform the presenting customer (beneficiary), so that he can ask the drawer to record stop payment

fact_checks.claim: If cheques are lost in transit or in the clearing process, the bank should immediately bring the same to the notice of the presenting customer (beneficiary)'s notice so that the customer can inform the drawer to record stop payment

Mizoram Co-operative Apex Bank Ltd and Paytm Payments Bank Ltd

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In November 1983, which body did RBI set up to introduce mechanised cheque processing and national clearing of cheques?

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records the National Clearing Cell (NCC), set up in November 1983 to introduce mechanised cheque processing and national clearing; MICR technology followed in March 1987.
solution.why_others_wrong: NPCI came in 2008; CCIL was established in 2001 for securities/forex/money market settlement; the National Grid Clearing House (Chennai) dates from 2023.
solution.final_answer: Option A: National Clearing Cell

30 Apr 2001: Clearing Corporation of India established

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An FCNR(B) depositor died on 10 March, before his deposit matured on 30 June. His heirs claimed the money on 30 August. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what interest is payable?

options.text: The contracted rate up to 10 March only, and nothing after the death
The RFC savings rate from 10 March to 30 August
The contracted rate for the whole period up to 30 August
The contracted rate up to 30 June, and simple interest at the rate operative on 30 June for 1 July–30 August

solution.explanation: If the depositor dies before maturity but the deposit is claimed after maturity, interest is paid at the contracted rate till maturity and simple interest at the applicable rate operative on the maturity date for the period beyond maturity. (The RFC savings rate applies only if death occurs after maturity.)
steps: Death before maturity, claim after maturity
Contracted rate to 30 June; simple interest at rate on 30 June for the overdue period
solution.why_others_wrong: Interest does not stop at death; the RFC savings rate applies when death is after maturity; the contracted rate does not run beyond maturity.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The contracted rate up to 30 June, and simple interest at the rate operative on 30 June for 1 July–30 August

fact_checks.claim: In case the depositor dies before the date of maturity of the deposit, but the amount of the deposit is claimed after the date of maturity, interest shall be paid at the contracted rate till the date of maturity and simple interest at the applicable rate operative on the date of maturity for the period for which the deposit remained with the bank beyond the date of maturity

In case of death of the depositor after the date of maturity of the deposit, the interest rate operative on the date of maturity in respect of savings deposit held under RFC Account Scheme shall be paid

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about premature withdrawal of FCNR(B) deposits under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025:
I. A bank must, on the depositor's request, permit premature withdrawal of an FCNR(B) deposit.
II. If the deposit is withdrawn before completing the minimum period of one year, no interest is paid.
III. A penalty must be levied when an NRI returning to India prematurely converts his FCNR(B) balance into an RFC account.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Banks must permit premature withdrawal of FCNR(B) deposits on request (I), and no interest is paid if the withdrawal is before the minimum stipulated period (II). No penalty is levied on premature conversion of FCNR(B) balances into RFC accounts by NRIs on return, so III is wrong (penalties do apply to conversion between FCNR(B) and NRE).
steps: III: false – conversion into RFC on return is penalty-free
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall, on request from the depositor, permit premature withdrawal of deposits under the FCNR(B) Scheme. If the premature withdrawal of FCNR(B) deposits takes place before completion of the minimum stipulated period ... no interest shall be paid
No penalties shall be levied in the case of premature conversion of balances held in FCNR(B) deposits into RFC Accounts by Non-Resident Indians on their return to India

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Two NRIs return to India for good and immediately ask their banks to convert NRE term deposits into Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) accounts: X's deposit has run for 8 months, Y's for 18 months. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what interest do they get on the NRE deposits?

options.text: X: the contracted rate less a penalty; Y: the contracted rate
X: at most the rate on RFC savings deposits; Y: the contracted rate — and no premature withdrawal penalty for either
X: nothing; Y: the RFC savings rate
Both: the contracted rate, plus a penalty for premature withdrawal

solution.explanation: If the NRE deposit has not run for the minimum period of one year, interest on conversion into RFC is paid at a rate not exceeding the RFC savings rate (X); otherwise at the contracted rate (Y). No premature withdrawal penalty is levied on NRE deposits converted into RFC accounts.
solution.why_others_wrong: No penalty applies to NRE → RFC conversion; X is not denied interest; Y gets the contracted rate.
solution.final_answer: Option B: X: at most the rate on RFC savings deposits; Y: the contracted rate — and no premature withdrawal penalty for either

fact_checks.claim: If an NRE account holder, immediately on return to India, requests for conversion of the NRE term deposit into Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account ... If the NRE deposit has not run for a minimum period of one year, interest shall be paid at a rate not exceeding the rate payable on savings deposits held in RFC accounts. In all other cases, interest shall be paid at the contracted rate
No penalty shall be levied for premature withdrawal of NRE term deposits for conversion into RFC account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the DEA Fund procedures in RBI's Commercial Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025:
I. A bank may designate up to 10 officers as authorised signatories to operate its DEA Fund account jointly.
II. A bank submits only one consolidated claim per month to the Fund, during the first 10 working days.
III. Interest payable from the Fund on a claim accrues from the date the depositor opened the account.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Banks may designate a maximum of 10 officers as joint authorised signatories (I) and submit one consolidated claim a month during the first 10 working days (II). Interest from the Fund accrues only from the date the balance was transferred to the Fund to the date of payment, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – from date of transfer to the Fund
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall designate up to a maximum of 10 officers as authorised signatories to operate the bank's DEA Fund account jointly
A bank shall ... submit claim from the Fund in e-Kuber system during the first 10 working days of every month. A bank shall submit only one consolidated claim per month
The interest payable, if any, from the Fund on a claim shall accrue only from the date on which the balance in an account was transferred to the Fund to the date of payment

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following changes to the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934 announced by RBI in 2026:
I. Coastal Local Area Bank Limited was included in the Second Schedule (Gazette of 11 August 2026).
II. Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A. ceased to be a banking company within the meaning of Section 36A(2) of the Banking Regulation Act and was excluded from the Second Schedule (Gazette of 2 July 2026).
III. Paytm Payments Bank Limited was included in the Second Schedule (Gazette of 7 September 2026).
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Coastal Local Area Bank was included by notification of 28 July 2026, published on 11 August 2026 (I). Rabobank, a foreign bank, ceased to be a banking company under Section 36A(2) and was excluded from the Second Schedule, both notified on 24 June 2026 and published on 2 July 2026 (II). Paytm Payments Bank was excluded from, not included in, the Second Schedule by the notification published on 7 September 2026, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – Paytm Payments Bank was excluded
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Coastal Local Area Bank Limited has been included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 vide Notification ... dated July 28, 2026 and published in the Gazette of India ... dated August 11, 2026

Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A. has ceased to be a banking company within the meaning of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 vide Notification ... dated June 24, 2026 which is published in the Gazette of India ... dated July 02, 2026
Coöperatieve Rabobank U.A. has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 vide Notification ... dated June 24, 2026

Paytm Payments Bank Limited has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 vide Notification ... dated July 31, 2026 and published in the Gazette of India ... dated September 07, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Dr. Nagesh Kumar, a Government-appointed member of the Monetary Policy Committee, heads which institution?

options.text: Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID), New Delhi
National Council of Applied Economic Research

steps: Dr. Nagesh Kumar → ISID, New Delhi
solution.why_others_wrong: DSE is Prof. Ram Singh's institution; NCAER and ISI are not named.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID), New Delhi

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, what floor applies to interest rates on fixed rate loans of tenor below three years?

options.text: They must equal the policy repo rate plus 2 per cent
They cannot be lower than the benchmark rate for a similar tenor
There is no floor; banks may price them freely
They cannot be lower than the Bank Rate

solution.explanation: Banks may offer fixed or floating rates, but interest on fixed rate loans of tenor below three years must not be less than the benchmark rate for similar tenor; and there can be no lending below the benchmark for loans linked to it.
steps: Fixed rate, tenor < 3 years → ≥ benchmark for similar tenor
solution.why_others_wrong: No repo-plus-2% rule exists; there is a floor; the Bank Rate is not the reference.
solution.final_answer: Option B: They cannot be lower than the benchmark rate for a similar tenor

fact_checks.claim: Interest rates on fixed rate loans of tenor below three years shall not be less than the benchmark rate for similar tenor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the MCLR system in RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, the spread over MCLR consists of business strategy and credit risk premium. What restriction applies to these components?

options.text: They must each be at least 1 percentage point
They can be negative to win large borrowers
They can be positive or zero, but cannot be negative
They must be identical for all borrowers

solution.explanation: The spread components — business strategy and credit risk premium — must have either a positive value or be zero; they cannot be negative, so loans cannot be priced below MCLR through a negative spread.
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no 1-point minimum; negative spreads are barred; spreads vary across borrowers by risk.
solution.final_answer: Option C: They can be positive or zero, but cannot be negative

fact_checks.claim: The components of the spread i.e. business strategy and Credit risk premium shall have either a positive value or be zero. In other words, the spread components cannot be negative

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the liquidity management framework of 30 September 2025, how much advance notice does RBI ordinarily give market participants before conducting a repo/reverse repo liquidity operation?

options.text: At least one day, though it may announce an operation on the same day when circumstances warrant
No notice; all operations are announced at the start of the auction window
At least one fortnight, matching the reserve maintenance period

solution.explanation: To reduce uncertainty about the tenor, quantum and timing of operations, RBI gives participants at least one day's advance notice, while retaining the option of same-day operations when warranted.
steps: Ordinarily ≥ 1 day notice; same-day possible when warranted
solution.why_others_wrong: One week or a fortnight is not the rule; operations are not announced only at the window.
solution.final_answer: Option A: At least one day, though it may announce an operation on the same day when circumstances warrant

fact_checks.claim: the Reserve Bank will provide sufficient advance notice to market participants, at least by one day, while conducting any such liquidity operation. However, when circumstances warrant, the Reserve Bank would conduct operations by announcing on the same day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At its 57th meeting (29 September–1 October 2025), the MPC kept the repo rate at 5.50% even though inflation had turned 'even more benign'. What reason did it give?

options.text: Inflation was above the upper tolerance limit
It was prudent to let the front-loaded monetary policy actions and recent fiscal measures play out and wait for clarity on trade uncertainties
The Government had asked RBI not to cut rates
Liquidity was in deficit, so a cut would not be transmitted

solution.explanation: The MPC noted that the impact of front-loaded rate cuts and recent fiscal measures (including GST rationalisation) was still playing out and trade uncertainties were unfolding, so it considered it prudent to wait before charting the next course; it continued with the neutral stance.
steps: Space existed, but waited for past actions to play out
solution.why_others_wrong: Inflation was low (2.1% in August 2025); the Government does not direct the MPC's vote; liquidity was not cited.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It was prudent to let the front-loaded monetary policy actions and recent fiscal measures play out and wait for clarity on trade uncertainties

fact_checks.claim: the MPC noted that the impact of the front-loaded monetary policy actions and the recent fiscal measures is still playing out. The trade related uncertainties are also unfolding. The MPC, therefore, considered it prudent to wait for the impact of policy actions to play out and greater clarity to emerge

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the liquidity management framework of 30 September 2025, which participants were given access to the SDF, overnight reverse repo operations and all repo operations irrespective of tenor?

solution.explanation: The revised framework allows Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) access to the SDF, overnight reverse repo operations and all repo operations, irrespective of tenor. (They had been allowed into all repo operations from March 2025.)
steps: SPDs → SDF + overnight reverse repo + all repos
solution.why_others_wrong: NBFCs, mutual funds and payment operators are not LAF participants.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Standalone Primary Dealers

fact_checks.claim: Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) will have access to SDF, overnight reverse repo operations, and all repo operations, irrespective of their tenor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about MPC decisions in 2025:
I. At its April 2025 meeting the MPC changed the stance from neutral to accommodative.
II. At its August 2025 meeting the MPC unanimously kept the repo rate at 5.50% and all members decided to continue with the neutral stance.
III. At its meeting ending 1 October 2025 the MPC changed the stance to accommodative.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: April 2025: along with a 25 bps cut, the MPC changed the stance from neutral to accommodative (I). August 2025: unanimous pause at 5.50% with all members for neutral (II). October 2025: the MPC continued with the neutral stance, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Moreover, it also decided to change the stance from neutral to accommodative
the MPC unanimously voted to keep the repo rate unchanged ... all members decided to continue with the neutral stance
The MPC also decided to continue with the neutral stance

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Compare the members who attended the MPC meeting of February 2025 (Malhotra, Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Ram Singh, Rajiv Ranjan, M. Rajeshwar Rao) with those of February 2026. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All six members were the same
Two of the three Government-appointed members had changed
The three Government-appointed members were the same, while Dr. Poonam Gupta and Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya had replaced Dr. Rajiv Ranjan and Shri M. Rajeshwar Rao
Dr. Poonam Gupta had replaced Prof. Ram Singh as a Government-appointed member

solution.explanation: Both meetings had Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Shri Saugata Bhattacharya and Prof. Ram Singh as the external members (appointed for four years from October 2024). The RBI side changed: in February 2026 the members were Governor Malhotra, Deputy Governor Dr. Poonam Gupta and Executive Director Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya (nominated by the Central Board), in place of Shri Rajeshwar Rao and Dr. Rajiv Ranjan.
steps: RBI members: Gupta and Bhattacharyya in place of Rao and Ranjan
solution.why_others_wrong: The RBI members changed; the external members did not; Dr. Gupta is an RBI (Deputy Governor) member.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The three Government-appointed members were the same, while Dr. Poonam Gupta and Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya had replaced Dr. Rajiv Ranjan and Shri M. Rajeshwar Rao

fact_checks.claim: The MPC members Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Shri Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh, Dr. Rajiv Ranjan, and Shri M. Rajeshwar Rao attended the meeting (February 5 to 7, 2025)

attended by all the members – Dr. Nagesh Kumar ...; Shri Saugata Bhattacharya ...; Professor Ram Singh ...; Dr. Poonam Gupta, Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy and Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya, Executive Director (the officer of the Reserve Bank nominated by the Central Board under Section 45ZB(2)(c))

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about loans exempted from the benchmark-linked pricing rules (Base Rate, MCLR, external benchmark) in RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025:
I. Advances to a bank's depositors against their own deposits are exempt.
II. Advances to the bank's own employees, including retired employees, are exempt.
III. Loans under Government schemes that prescribe the interest rate must still be priced at or above the bank's MCLR.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Directions exempt, among others, loans under Government schemes where the bank must charge the scheme's rate, WCTL/FITL under restructuring, refinance-scheme loans (to the extent refinanced), advances to depositors against their own deposits (I), advances to employees including retired employees (II), and advances to the CEO/whole-time directors. Scheme loans are exempt, so III is wrong.
steps: III: scheme-rate loans are exempt – false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The following types of loans shall be exempted from the provisions contained under paragraphs 10 to 41 of these Directions: (1) Loans covered by schemes specially formulated by Government of India wherein a bank has to charge interest rates as per the scheme ... (i) Advances to banks' depositors against their own deposits. (ii) Advances to banks' own employees including retired employees

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's USD/INR buy/sell swap auction of December 2025 (USD 5 billion, 36 months):
I. Bids were quoted as the premium, in paisa, that banks were willing to pay RBI for the tenor of the swap.
II. It was a multiple-price auction: successful bids were accepted at their own quoted premium.
III. Bids were arranged in ascending order of premium, and those below the cut-off were accepted.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Participants bid the premium (paisa, two decimals) they would pay RBI (I); the auction was multiple-price, with successful bids accepted at their quoted premium (II). Bids were arranged in descending order, and those at or above the cut-off premium succeeded while lower bids were rejected, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – descending order; bids at/above cut-off succeed
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'II only' leaves out the true statement I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The market participants would be required to place their bids in terms of the premium that they are willing to pay to the Reserve Bank for the tenor of the swap, expressed in paisa terms up to two decimal places ... The auction would be a multiple-price based auction, i.e., successful bids will get accepted at their respective quoted premium

all the bids would be arranged in descending order of the swap premium quoted ... Successful bidders would be those who have placed their bids at or above the cut-off premium. All bids lower than the cut-off premium would be rejected

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's liquidity framework as it stands in November 2026:
I. The symmetric corridor finalised in September 2025 is retained, with the SDF and MSF 25 bps on either side of the repo rate.
II. The weighted average call rate remains the operating target, while RBI also tracks rates in other overnight money market segments.
III. The 14-day variable rate repo/reverse repo remains the main operation for managing transient liquidity.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The September 2025 framework retained the symmetric corridor (I) and the WACR as operating target, with RBI also tracking other overnight segments (II). The 14-day VRR/VRRR was discontinued as the main operation; transient liquidity is managed mainly through 7-day operations, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – 7-day operations are now the main tool
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The existing symmetric corridor system is retained, with policy repo rate at the middle of the corridor and standing deposit facility (SDF) and marginal standing facility (MSF), which are 25 bps on either side of the policy repo rate ... The overnight weighted average call rate (WACR) will continue to be the operating target of the monetary policy. The Reserve Bank will, however, continue to keep track of rates in other overnight money market segments
The 14-day variable rate repo (VRR)/ variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) operation will be discontinued as the main operation for managing short-term/transient liquidity

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At its 54th meeting (7–9 April 2025), the MPC cut the policy repo rate by 25 bps. To what level?

solution.explanation: In April 2025 the MPC unanimously cut the repo rate by 25 bps to 6.00%, with the SDF at 5.75% and the MSF and Bank Rate at 6.25%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.25% was the rate after February; 5.75% is the SDF; 5.50% came in June.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 6.00%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Why did the MPC opt for a larger 50 bps repo cut in June 2025, according to its resolution?

options.text: Inflation had risen above the 6% upper tolerance limit
The Government had cut the fiscal deficit target
The changed growth-inflation dynamics called for frontloading rate cuts to stimulate private consumption and investment
The US Federal Reserve had cut rates by 50 bps

solution.explanation: The MPC said it was imperative to stimulate domestic private consumption and investment, and the changed growth-inflation dynamics called for not only continuing easing but also frontloading the rate cuts to support growth.
steps: Benign inflation + need to support growth → frontload (50 bps)
solution.why_others_wrong: Inflation was low, not above 6%; fiscal and Fed actions were not the reason given.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The changed growth-inflation dynamics called for frontloading rate cuts to stimulate private consumption and investment

fact_checks.claim: This changed growth-inflation dynamics calls for not only continuing with the policy easing but also frontloading the rate cuts to support growth. Accordingly, the MPC voted to reduce the policy repo rate by 50 bps to 5.50 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In RBI's overnight Variable Rate Repo auction of 21 October 2026 (notified ₹50,000 crore; repo rate 5.50%), bids of ₹93,241 crore were received and ₹50,007 crore was allotted at a cut-off rate of 5.52%. What does this indicate?

options.text: Banks had surplus funds, so the auction was undersubscribed
RBI lent at the SDF rate because demand was weak
The auction failed and RBI lent nothing
Banks' demand for funds exceeded the amount RBI offered, so the cut-off settled slightly above the repo rate

solution.why_others_wrong: It was oversubscribed, not under; the rate was above repo, not the SDF; ₹50,007 crore was allotted.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Banks' demand for funds exceeded the amount RBI offered, so the cut-off settled slightly above the repo rate

fact_checks.claim: Tenor 1-day; Notified Amount 50,000; Total amount of bids received 93,241; Amount allotted 50,007; Cut off Rate (%) 5.52

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the MPC's decision of 7 February 2025:

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's table of CRR changes:
I. CRR fell below 10% for the first time in that reform phase on 25 October 1997, when it was cut to 9.75%.
II. CRR was raised to 11% on 29 August 1998.
III. CRR first fell below 5% only in 2003.
Which of the above is/are correct?

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's table shows CRR at 9.5% from 6 November 1999, 9% from 20 November 1999, 8.5% from 8 April 2000 and 8% from 22 April 2000. How much cash was released for a bank with NDTL of ₹10,000 crore between November 1999 and end-April 2000?

solution.explanation: CRR fell from 9.5% to 8%, a cut of 1.5 percentage points: 1.5% × ₹10,000 crore = ₹150 crore released.

solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹150 crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's table, on 1 July 1974 the SLR was raised to 33%. What happened to the CRR on the same day?

solution.explanation: RBI's table shows SLR raised to 33% and CRR reduced to 5% (from 7%) with effect from 1 July 1974.
solution.why_others_wrong: CRR was cut, not raised; 3% applied before 1973; 15% came in 1989.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It was cut from 7% to 5%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's table shows SLR at 28% from 28 August 1970 and 33% from 1 July 1974. For a bank with DTL of ₹2,000 crore, by how much did its required SLR holdings rise between these dates (DTL unchanged)?

solution.explanation: SLR rose by 5 percentage points (28% → 33%): 5% × ₹2,000 crore = ₹100 crore of additional SLR assets.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹50 crore uses 2.5%; ₹660 crore and ₹560 crore are total requirements at 33% and 28%.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹100 crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Following the MPC's repo rate cut of April 2025, at what level did the Bank Rate stand?

solution.concept: Bank Rate aligned with the MSF
solution.explanation: The Bank Rate moves with the MSF rate, 25 bps above the repo rate. With the repo at 6.00% in April 2025, the MSF rate and Bank Rate were 6.25%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.00% was the repo; 6.50% the Bank Rate after February 2025; 5.75% the SDF in April.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 6.25%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's table, the Bank Rate reached 6% for the first time on:

solution.explanation: The Bank Rate went 5% (26 September 1964) → 6% (17 February 1965); it was cut to 5% on 2 March 1968 and restored to 6% on 9 January 1971.
solution.why_others_wrong: 26 Sep 1964 was 5%; 9 Jan 1971 was a return to 6%; 2 Mar 1968 was a cut to 5%.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 17 February 1965

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the liquidity management framework of September 2025, how much can an individual bank draw under the Marginal Standing Facility, whose rate is the same as the Bank Rate?

options.text: Up to 2% of NDTL only, with no use of excess SLR
Against its excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of its NDTL (as at the end of the second preceding fortnight) below the stipulated SLR

solution.explanation: The annex to the framework says banks can draw MSF funds against their excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of NDTL outstanding at the end of the second preceding fortnight, below the stipulated SLR.
steps: MSF = excess SLR + dip of up to 2% of NDTL
solution.why_others_wrong: Excess SLR also counts; MSF is collateralised; 1% was the 2011 limit.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Against its excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of its NDTL (as at the end of the second preceding fortnight) below the stipulated SLR

fact_checks.claim: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) | Individual banks can draw funds against their excess SLR holdings + up to 2 per cent of their respective NDTL outstanding as at the end of the second preceding fortnight, below the stipulated SLR

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
The Bank Rate was 6.50% after the MPC decision of February 2025. After the June 2025 decision it was 5.75%. Consider:
I. The Bank Rate fell by 75 bps between these two decisions.
II. The Bank Rate moved automatically with the MSF rate as the repo rate was cut.
III. The Bank Rate remained 50 bps above the repo rate throughout.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: 6.50 − 5.75 = 0.75 → 75 bps (I). The Bank Rate is aligned with the MSF rate and changes automatically with it (II). The MSF/Bank Rate is 25 bps above the repo rate (6.50 vs 6.25; 5.75 vs 5.50), so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate to 5.75 per cent
This rate has been aligned with the MSF rate and, changes automatically as and when the MSF rate changes alongside policy repo rate changes

questions.question_text: According to the December 2025 MPC resolution, what was core inflation excluding gold in October 2025, and how much did the rise in precious metal prices add to underlying inflation?

solution.why_others_wrong: 60–70 bps was the February 2026 figure; the other pairs are not from this resolution.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Governor's statement of 7 October 2026 cited sugar as one item behind broad-based food price pressures. What did it say about sugar prices?

options.text: They fell 34% because of a bumper crop
They were unchanged due to export restrictions
They rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August, before retreating in September

solution.explanation: Sugar prices rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August on a tight demand-supply balance and precautionary stocking; Government measures (export restrictions, stock limits, duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar) eased them, and prices retreated in September.
solution.why_others_wrong: Prices rose, not fell; they did not double; they were not unchanged.
solution.final_answer: Option D: They rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August, before retreating in September

fact_checks.claim: Sugar prices rose by about 34 per cent from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August, due to tight demand-supply balance and precautionary stocking ... Prices have since retreated gradually in September

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The WPI (base 2022-23) for all commodities was 110.8 in August 2026 and 112.5 in September 2026, when year-on-year WPI inflation was 11.39% (9.92% in August). Which statement is correct?

options.text: The index rose about 1.5% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by about 1.5 percentage points
The index fell month-on-month while year-on-year inflation rose
The index rose about 1.7% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by 1.7 percentage points

solution.explanation: Month-on-month: 112.5 ÷ 110.8 − 1 ≈ 1.53%. Year-on-year inflation rose from 9.92% to 11.39%, i.e. 1.47 percentage points. The 11.39% compares September 2026 with September 2025, not with August.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11.39% is the y-o-y rate; the index rose; 1.7 points is the index-point change, not a percentage.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The index rose about 1.5% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by about 1.5 percentage points

questions.question_text: RBI provides a Standing Liquidity Facility to Standalone Primary Dealers at the prevailing repo rate. From 2 April 2025, to what level did it raise the aggregate limit of this facility?
